domain.name: Noru cards
domain.purpose: A synthetic rule-learning micro-domain with no required prior subject knowledge.
domain.readingOrder: Represent a card as band/mark/count, for example ava/plain/2. Apply operation sequences from left to right.

rules.name: flip
rules.text: flip changes ava to bor or bor to ava. It does not change mark or count.

rules.name: echo on plain
rules.text: If the card is plain, echo changes plain to ring and advances count: 1 to 2, 2 to 3, and 3 to 1. Band does not change.

rules.name: echo on ring
rules.text: If the card is ring, echo changes ring to plain and leaves count unchanged. Band does not change.

rules.name: sequence
rules.text: For two or more operations, use the result of each operation as the input to the next operation, reading left to right.

rules.name: compatibility
rules.text: Two cards are compatible when either they have the same band and their counts total 4, or they have different bands and the same mark. Exception: two ring cards are never compatible.

glossary.meaning: The first text label: ava or bor.
The second text label: plain or ring.
A relationship determined only by R5 after any requested operations are complete.

reasoning: R2 applies because the card is plain.
plain becomes ring and 3 advances to 1.

workedExamples.prompt: Apply echo, then flip, to ava/ring/2.
reasoning: R3 changes ring to plain and leaves 2 unchanged.
R1 then changes ava to bor.
The exception applies because both marks are ring.

practiceItems.prompt: Apply flip to bor/plain/1 and explain what stays unchanged.
Apply echo to ava/plain/2 and name the rule branch used.
Apply echo to bor/ring/3 and name the rule branch used.
Apply echo to ava/plain/3 and explain the count result.
Apply flip, echo, then echo to ava/plain/1.
Decide whether ava/plain/1 and ava/ring/3 are compatible and cite the decisive R5 condition.
Decide whether ava/plain/2 and bor/plain/3 are compatible and cite the decisive R5 condition.
Decide whether ava/ring/2 and bor/ring/2 are compatible and explain whether the exception changes the result.
